findings.finding: The new precedence text says 'An index or a planned baseline keeps its mode whatever the licence'. For an index that matches the checker: INDEX_ONLY admits every repository outcome, and the probe giving an index a denied licence was accepted. For a planned baseline it overstates the rule. REUSE_OUTCOMES admits PLANNED_BASELINE only with DEFAULT_ALLOWED or PLANNED_UNRESOLVED, and the probe of letta as a planned baseline with no licence was rejected. No current record is affected: the four planned baselines are langfuse (PLANNED_UNRESOLVED), langgraph, promptfoo and letta (all DEFAULT_ALLOWED).
findings.requiredChange: None required. Optional: reword to 'An index keeps its mode whatever the licence; a planned baseline keeps its mode when its licence outcome is default-allowed or unresolved (NOASSERTION); in both cases the licence ceiling binds.'

findings.finding:
Residual limits. None affects the current data.
(a) 'jdoe at example dot com', with a spelled-out dot and no brackets, is not matched. All bracketed and dotted-domain forms are now rejected.
(b) The licenceStatedInPaper derivation tests whether 'NOT_FOUND' and 'licen' both appear anywhere in a status detail. A truthful detail such as 'VERIFIED for the code; NOT_FOUND for the corpus; licence stated as MIT' would therefore force the flag to false.
(c) A detail must use the token 'NOT_FOUND'; a lower-case 'licence not found' is rejected. This fails closed, which is acceptable.
(d) Rejecting 'available at <site>.com' is accepted as a deliberate fail-closed rule.
(e) Bare names and free-form prompt residue remain review-only, as accepted earlier.
findings.requiredChange: None required. Optional: match 'dot' as a separator in the 'x at domain' rule, and test for 'NOT_FOUND for (a|the) licen' rather than co-occurrence of the two words.

dispositions.evidence: LICENSE_BLOCKED now says it takes precedence over REFERENCE_DESIGN unless the licence outcome is default-allowed, an allowed exception or open content. This matches REUSE_OUTCOMES and the data: phoenix, DeLM, mattermost, Self-Harness and OPHSD are LICENSE_BLOCKED, and claudes-c-compiler (open content) is REFERENCE_DESIGN. The probe putting phoenix in REFERENCE_DESIGN is still rejected. The '(review R2-2)' tag is gone. The planned-baseline half of the last sentence overstates the checker rule (R4-1, NOTE).

licenceStatedInPaper is now derived from the licence checks ('licen' matches either spelling). The probes rejected: true for MASS, true for VeriHarness, a detail claiming the licence verified while the flag is false, the 'license' spelling without a detail, a removed or licence-free detail, and a paper with no licence check. A coherent detail-plus-flag pair was accepted. Every seed paper has exactly one licence check, and all eight derive to false, which matches the round-3 grep of the PDFs. The '(at)', '( at )', '[at]', '{at}' and '(dot)' forms are rejected. The DESIGN_REFERENCE_ONLY wording now matches ceiling(), and DENY_MISSING_LICENSE explains the null licence. Rejecting 'available at <site>' is accepted as deliberate. Residual edges are in R4-2.
